summary:
Abandoned Yet Not Forgotten is a student-friendly website by Team Echoes Beyond (Satyapragyan Mohanty and Krishna Das) for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It is for educational purposes only.

The challenge: Since the 1960s NASA has left hardware on the Moon, on Mars and in deep space. We tell its story to school-age space fans by answering three questions: where is each machine, does it still work, and what did it make possible.

What we built:

A cinematic intro and a home page with a live Voyager 1 distance counter.
An archive of 23 machines, searchable by place and status. Only 5 still fully work.
An interactive “Where is it now?” map with a four-stop tour from the Moon outward.
A page for every machine, with its story, current status, Read more, a hands-on activity, NASA photos and a quiz question.
A debris simulator game, a quiz, a glossary of 26 space words and a printable teacher guide.

We also made a 7-slide PowerPoint and a README.
details:
What it does: A website on the hardware NASA left on the Moon, Mars and in deep space. It covers 23 machines, each with a status (still working, gone quiet, destroyed or came home). Visitors search the archive, tour an interactive map, and open a page for each machine with its story, NASA photos, a quiz question and a hands-on activity. There is also a debris game, a glossary and a teacher guide.

Benefits: It is free, needs no login, and works on phones and computers. Teachers get 23 low-cost activities.

Impact: To show students that missions don’t simply end, because their machines and discoveries are still out there, and to spark interest in space science.

Tools: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, canvas and SVG, Google Fonts, NASA’s public image library, and PptxGenJS for the slides.

Creativity: It asks “where is it now?” instead of listing achievements. A live Voyager 1 counter, a realistic debris simulator and real space photography make it feel like mission control.

Factors considered: Accuracy (current statuses checked against NASA on 15 November 2026), a student audience of roughly ages 10 to 15, safe activities, and easy access on any device.

Source Code (GitHub Repository):

[GitHub Repository](https://github.com/satyapragyanmohanty1-byte/Echoes_Beyond)

The repository contains the project's HTML, CSS, JavaScript and other supporting assets required to understand and run the application.
